headline: Ship {arm:atlas-m} on all traffic. It is the only candidate that clears every gate.
lede: Cheaper models win two of the five tasks, but routing traffic to them is blocked: both fail the speculation gate, and speculation bait shows up inside every task. Once a cheaper model clears that gate, routing would cut cost.

slots.text: **{arm:atlas-m} everywhere.** It passes the quality floor, every task-specific behavior and the latency budget on all five tasks.

**{arm:atlas-l}** has the best quality but misses the {criteria.p95.threshold} p95 latency budget on four of five tasks. **{arm:brisk-s}** and **{arm:open-70b}** speculate too often on bait prompts to pass the speculation gate.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion}: {weakest.value}, exactly at its {weakest.threshold} floor, with an interval that crosses it. A larger troubleshooting sample settles it before launch.

Test a speculation guard on {arm:brisk-s}. If it clears the speculation gate, route billing to {arm:brisk-s} and small talk to {arm:open-70b}, and the recommendation changes from one model to a routing plan.

method.text: Conversations sampled from September production logs and stratified by task. Speculation bait is a test category, not a traffic segment.

Overall quality is a rubric score from a judge calibrated against {judged.overall.calibration_ratings|int} human-graded conversations (agreement {judged.overall.agreement|pct}). Behaviors are graded pass or fail per conversation.
Normal intervals; behavior rates use the binomial standard error.
Measured tokens times list price, stated per 1,000 replies; blended cost weights tasks by September traffic.

sections.headline: {arm:atlas-m} passes every task; the cheapest passing model differs by task
sections.takeaway: Each cell checks overall quality, every task-specific behavior against its floor, and p95 latency. Amber means the score clears the floor but its interval crosses it.

sections.headline: {arm:brisk-s} and {arm:open-70b} decline speculation bait less often than the gate requires
sections.takeaway: Declining to speculate on bait prompts, with intervals; the floor is the dashed line.

sections.headline: {arm:atlas-l}'s tail latency exceeds the budget everywhere except small talk
sections.takeaway: Latency by task. Research is the slowest task because it includes a tool round trip.
sections.caption: Measured end to end from user message to final token, in staging.

explore.title: Change the gates and see which plan wins

controls.title: Every routed model must pass the speculation gate

explore.recomputes: Which candidates pass each task and the cheapest routing plan; turning off the speculation requirement makes routing to the cheaper models win.

durable_claims.text: Small concierge models fail the speculation gate rather than overall quality, which blocks routing to them; judge agreement here was {judged.overall.agreement|pct}.
